$comment: T2.9/T3.2 (PLAN-ci-time-budget, operator spec W). Measured cost per lane, read by
scripts/ci-runner/lanes.ts's shardPlan (its optional 4th argument) so a sharded lane
balances legs by real duration once one exists, instead of by scheduler `weight`.
'jobs' is each job's fixed cost (p90 minutes, setup through the first runner step);
'units' is each shard-plan unit id's own p90 in MILLISECONDS, keyed exactly as the
id appears in gates.lock.json (a quality-code check id) or in a test lane's own
enumerator (scripts/ci-runner/unit-enumerators.ts), for example 'pytest:tests/....py'.
SEEDED 2026-09-26 with 'concurrency' only (operator ruling D-W1: stay on GitHub Free,
20 concurrent jobs) -- 'jobs' and 'units' are empty until T3.2's
'budget_report.py --refresh' runs against real green CI data. An empty 'units' means
every shardPlan caller falls back to `weight` for every unit, so quality-code's plan
is unaffected until this file actually names one of its ids (see the selftest control
'shardPlan(durations: {}) is byte-identical to shardPlan() with no durations argument'
in scripts/gate-bind.ts).
T3.1's freshness check (scripts/gates/check-lane-budget.ts) reds when the TOP-LEVEL
'refreshed_at' is older than 14 days -- that field, plus 'jobs'/'units'/'defaultUnitMs',
is written ONLY by 'budget_report.py --refresh' (T3.2/T3.3).
'job_max_seconds' is a SEPARATE section, D-W2/T3.4's retirement of the old
job-timeout-baseline.json into this one file: check_job_timeout_headroom.py's own
baseline for the two direct (never lane-sharded) ci.yml jobs the lane-budget gate does
not cover, Validate Promotion and Stage Artifacts. It carries its OWN 'refreshed_at',
written ONLY by 'check_job_timeout_headroom.py --refresh' -- a shared timestamp would
let either refresh silently un-stale numbers the other half never re-measured.
'job_max_seconds.jobs[*].observed_max_seconds' is the worst observed wall time in
SECONDS (MIN_HEADROOM=1.5x that number must fit under the job's timeout-minutes),
migrated verbatim from job-timeout-baseline.json's last real refresh (run 32491717875,
see that retired file's own history for the full 'why one sample' account).
'defaultUnitMs' (hand-authored 2026-09-28, T3.1; --refresh preserves it verbatim). The
quality lanes price their units by gate id, and no test-runner artifact reports a gate
id, so these lanes carry one MEASURED per-unit figure each instead of per-gate p90s.
Source: the Actions jobs API (paginated; every job, not the first 100) for the 10 latest
completed pull_request runs of ci.yml, 36332829873..36370123947 (2026-09-27T16:19Z to
2026-09-28T02:31Z), success-only jobs as budget_report samples them. Derivation per lane:
defaultUnitMs = (p90 job wall minutes - jobs[lane] fixed minutes) x 60000 / unit count,
and for sharded quality-code the MAX of that over its 4 legs (leg 1: 8.8m / 23 units),
so no leg is priced below its own measurement. A lane with no 'jobs' entry has its fixed
cost folded into the figure (fixed 0 in the gate). Inputs, p90 wall / units: branch
8.5m / 9 (completed jobs: the job fails every PR run on check:ci-plan-implementation,
so it has no success sample), code legs 8.8/6.2/7.5/6.4m / 23/27/27/27, content
3.0m / 45, gate-tests 0.8m - 0.7m fixed / 6, go 7.6m / 17, i18n 5.1m / 40, packages
5.7m / 13, security 1.8m / 18, static 4.5m / 64, wiring 0.5m / 1, www-build 3.6m / 16.
These quality figures are not refreshed by any tool yet: re-derive them by the recipe above
when refreshed_at moves.
The SHARDED test lanes and quality-pytest (added 2026-09-30, T3.1 check 4) price a unit
with no 'units' entry at the p90 of that lane's own measured unit p90s, rounded UP to
100 ms, from the 2026-09-30T10:07:24Z refresh: quality-pytest 23385 ms over 526 files,
test-account-e2e 24293 over 99, test-renet-go 5446 over 86, test-renet-integration
153581 over 12, ops-tutorials 176960 over 18; test-e2e-workers takes the p90 of its
variantCosts wall spans (155063 over 105 variant-unit entries), not of the top-level
summed test durations (146818), because a leg prices from the wall spans. The default
exists so a NEW file enters priced like a typical unit of its lane instead of blocking
every plan; the next --refresh measures it and the default stops applying to it.
'unitParallelism' (hand-authored 2026-09-28, T3.1; --refresh preserves it): how many units
one leg runs at once, which is the CI runner's core count, not a chosen width. quality-pytest: 4.
Since 2026-10-05 (agent/plans/PLAN-prepush-full-cpu.md PF4) check_pytest.py's jobs() passes
`-n` = core_lease.granted_cores(), which on a CI leg (no runner grant) is the leg machine's
affinity count; ci-quality.yml sets no PYTEST_JOBS, and the leg's own profiler notice on job
108765034481 (Quality / Pytest (3/3)) reads 'peak 4.00 cores'. Still hand-authored: deriving it
from the runner's measured core count is budget_report.py's to do (PF6). Unit p90s stay
per-file SERIAL times; the gate divides by the workers and floors the leg at its largest xdist
group (a group runs on one worker).
'variantCosts' (T3.1; budget_report --refresh measures it from job logs and keeps the prior value for anything a sample did not measure; the gate reds when it is gone):
per-matrix-variant leg pricing for the lanes whose legs pay a cost no unit carries. Shape: {lane: {variant: {fixedMinutes,
legExtraMinutes?: {leg index: minutes}, units: {unit id: ms}}}}, where the variant is the first matrix value in the job's
display name ('fedora-43' in 'E2E Workers (fedora-43, 1/8)'). A leg costs fixedMinutes + its legExtraMinutes entry + the
sum of its units, each read from the variant's own 'units' first and the top-level 'units' second.
Source: the Actions jobs API and every success job's log for the 9 of the 10 newest 0923-1 ci.yml runs that ran the
Provision linux-amd64 jobs, all p90 by linear interpolation. test-e2e-workers: a unit's cost is its WALL span in the
log (its first test's start to the next file's first test, the last file to the E2E_SKIPPED line), not budget_report's
summed test durations, which leave out beforeAll/afterAll work (07-container-operations: 0.77m of tests, 3.23m of wall
on opensuse); fixedMinutes is the job wall minus every file's span, which is the steps before 'Run E2E Tests', the
globalSetup VM reset (renet ops up --force: 1.5m median on debian, 3.1-4.1m on fedora, opensuse and oracle), the renet,
RustFS and datastore setup after it, and the post steps; legExtraMinutes '1' is the span of 12a/12b/12d/13b, which
ct-tests.yml adds to leg 1 of the two full-integration distros. ops-tutorials: fixedMinutes is the job wall minus the
tutorial durations (every step outside the tutorials, from runner setup through ops up and the post steps, the same on
every shard, so no legExtraMinutes), and the tutorials' own costs are the top-level units. Checked against job_p90_minutes: every E2E Workers leg within
0.83m and every OPS Provision leg within 0.8m (npx tsx scripts/gates/check-lane-budget.ts --table).
'rebalanceConstraints' (hand-authored 2026-09-28; --refresh preserves it verbatim): the placement rules
`check-lane-budget.ts --rebalance <lane>` must honour, each with the reason it exists. 'together' puts its units on one
leg, 'onLeg' pins a unit to a leg, 'notOnLeg' keeps a unit off one. quality-pytest needs no entry: its xdist groups come
from the gate's own mutex model and are indivisible there. The gate reds a committed plan that breaks a rule, and
--rebalance refuses one it cannot satisfy.
